description: We are Gabriel, Ian and Pedro, we are very interested in NASA and astronomy, and we’ve come to the NASA Space Apps Challenge to expand our knowledge and have fun completing the challenge.
summary: Our project addresses the first challenge by telling the stories of retired and lost NASA missions across space, with a primary focus on Mars. We developed an interactive game where players locate these silent probes and uncover their history in an engaging, educational way. This matters because much of today's everyday technology stems from these missions, yet they are rarely discussed. Their legacy deserves to be remembered and brought back into our conversations.
details: Our project is entirely based on the 1st challenge, it is a Scratch game, where you control a rover on Mars and find some scraps of other mission, so then you discover their history in an enganging and educational way. You control the rover with A (to go left), D (to go right) and W (to jump). The project is made for people who don't want to spend time reading articles or studying these stories in a lame way, here, you learn the story of these missions while entertaining yourself. We used paint.net and piskel to make the appearence of the game and used Scratch to program (Scratch uses block-based programming) and Google Gemini (for deep researching). This project is creative because it stimulates people to learn more about these missions and bring it back on conversations in a educational and entertaining way.
